rationales: The endoplasmic reticulum is not where ribosomes are produced.
The nucleoid is the DNA-containing region in prokaryotic cells.
The nucleolus produces ribosomal components and assembles ribosomal subunits.
A nuclear pore allows transport between the nucleus and cytoplasm but does not produce ribosomes.
Chloroplasts are green plastids containing chlorophyll.
Chromoplasts contain pigments other than chlorophyll and are coloured.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids, often involved in storage.
Etioplasts are immature plastids that develop in darkness.
Most transpiration occurs through the stomata.
Mesophyll is involved in gas exchange and water evaporation, but is not the main exit route for water vapour.
The cuticle allows only a small amount of transpiration.
Lenticels account for only a small amount of transpiration, mainly in woody stems.
Group O is generally the universal red-cell donor, not the universal recipient.
Group AB individuals are universal recipients for red-cell transfusions in the ABO system.
Group B individuals are not universal recipients.
Group A individuals are not universal recipients.
Microbiology is the study of microorganisms.
Histology is the microscopic study of tissues.
Biology is the general study of life.
Zoology is the study of animals.
A hypothesis is a tentative explanation of observations.
A theory is a well-supported explanation based on substantial evidence.
A law describes a consistent pattern or relationship in nature.
Deductions are conclusions drawn from premises or evidence, not tentative explanations of observations.
G1 is mainly a period of cell growth and normal activity before DNA replication.
DNA replication, which duplicates chromosomes, occurs during S phase.
G2 follows DNA replication and prepares the cell for division.
G0 is a non-dividing state outside the active cell cycle.
In the five-kingdom classification commonly used in this context, algae are placed in Protista.
Fungi include organisms such as mushrooms and yeasts, not algae.
Protista includes many algae in the classification used in school biology.
Monera includes prokaryotes such as bacteria.
The chukar partridge is the national bird of Pakistan.
The pigeon is not Pakistan’s national bird.
The parrot is not Pakistan’s national bird.
The crow is not Pakistan’s national bird.
DNA is a component of chromosomes, but chromosomes also contain proteins.
RNA is not the principal material composing chromosomes.
Chromosomes are composed of DNA and proteins.
RNA and protein are not the principal components of chromosomes.
Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane, not general movement against a concentration gradient.
Diffusion proceeds from higher concentration to lower concentration.
Facilitated diffusion also moves substances down their concentration gradient, using membrane proteins.
Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient, from lower to higher concentration, using energy.
Lipase breaks down fats.
Amylase breaks down starch.
Proteases break down proteins, not starch.
Trypsin is a protease that digests proteins.
Stomata typically cover about 1–2% of the leaf surface in the textbook estimate.
The standard estimate is not 1–3%.
The standard estimate is not 1–4%.
The standard estimate is not 1–5%.
Ingestion is the taking of food into the mouth.
Mastication is the grinding and chewing of food by the teeth.
Lubrication is the moistening of food, chiefly by saliva.
Digestion is the broader breakdown of food into simpler substances.
An organelle is a specialised structure within a cell, not a group of similar cells.
A tissue is a group of similar cells performing the same function.
An organ consists of different tissues working together.
An organ system consists of organs working together.
